# Intake Brief — LP-0MTTPXHTI0081WIR: Adopt structured summarization prompt for proxy compaction (R1)

## Problem Statement
Proxy-side compaction summarization uses a minimal open-ended prompt, producing lower-quality summaries than Pi's structured format. Adopting Pi's structured prompt will close the single largest quality gap (proxy 5/10 vs Pi 9/10 on summarization) identified in the compaction comparison.

## Users
- **Proxy operator / local-model user** — benefits from higher-quality middle-turn summaries that preserve decisions and next steps.
- **Agent-framework consumer whose session was compacted** — resumes work with a summary that clearly states goal, progress, and critical context.

### User Stories
- As a proxy operator, I want compacted sessions to retain a structured summary (Goal, Progress, Decisions, Next Steps, Critical Context) so that follow-up prompts continue correctly without re-explaining prior work.
- As a developer resuming after compaction, I want the summary to preserve constraints, key decisions, and file operations so that I don't lose prior context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 — Structured prompt sections:** `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (consumed by `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`) uses a structured format with sections: Goal, Constraints & Preferences, Progress (Done / In Progress / Blocked), Key Decisions, Next Steps, Critical Context, and File Operations (`<read-files>` / `<modified-files>` XML sections).
- [ ] **AC2 — Guard rails:** The prompt includes the same guard rails as Pi: `Do NOT continue the conversation. Do NOT respond to any questions.` (or semantically equivalent wording).
- [ ] **AC3 — No regression in compaction tests:** All existing compaction tests continue to pass (`proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_dry_run.py`).
- [ ] **AC4 — Rationale comment:** The prompt change is documented with a brief rationale comment in code (e.g., above `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `provider.py`, referencing Pi's `SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT` and the gap analysis).
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite / docs:** Full project test suite passes with the change; any related docs/code comments affected by the prompt change are updated.

## Constraints
- Prompt-engineering change only — no summarizer logic, retry, or config-schema changes in this item (R2/R3 are separate).
- Model is Qwen3 via local llama-server; `max_tokens` remains 512 (configurable via `compaction_config`).
- Summarizer remains fail-open; HTTP/timeout behavior unchanged.

## Existing State
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is a short open-ended prompt ("Summarise the middle portion... Preserve essential instructions... Omit routine back-and-forth...").
- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py:build_local_summarizer` imports that prompt and sends it as the system message with transcript as user message.
- Pi's `SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT` (in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`) is a highly structured multi-section prompt that scores 9/10 vs proxy's 5/10.

## Desired Change
- Replace `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` with a Pi-matching structured prompt (Goal; Constraints & Preferences; Progress — Done/In Progress/Blocked; Key Decisions; Next Steps; Critical Context; File Operations) plus the `Do NOT continue / Do NOT respond` guard rails and a short rationale comment linking to the design doc.

## Key Files
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Defines `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `compaction_config()`; needs prompt replacement + rationale comment.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — Imports and uses the prompt; no logic change expected but verify import path still resolves.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py` — Validates summarizer construction and HTTP call shape.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py` — Asserts `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is a non-empty string and wires into `compaction_config`.
- `docs/session-compaction-pi-comparison.md` — Design doc that identified R1 and benchmarks the gap.

## Related Work
- **Parent:** LP-0MTT890RO000AEQM — Compare Pi and proxy compaction approaches (completed/in_review) — source of R1–R7 roadmap.
- **Siblings (same roadmap):** LP-0MTTPXI1Y003YFOU (R2 file-ops), LP-0MTTPXIAB0031AC4 (R3 retry), LP-0MTTPXIIX005Y0Z9 (R5 incremental) — coordinate to avoid overlap; R1 is prompt-only, others add logic.
- **Potentially related docs:** `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` (planner/trigger), `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (routing/compaction config).
- **Potentially related work items:** LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD (proxy proactive compaction — completed), LP-0MTGBOOJY004OWPI (core summarization compaction).

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk — Summary verbosity vs 512-token budget:** Structured format may use more tokens; mitigate by keeping section prompts concise and monitoring `max_tokens` headroom. *Assumption: 512 remains sufficient for a structured summary of middle turns.*
- **Risk — Downstream prompt sensitivity:** Downstream LLM may be sensitive to prompt format; mitigate by matching Pi's proven wording closely.
- **Risk — Test brittleness to prompt text:** Few tests assert on prompt content (only non-empty/string checks); prompt change is safe. Verify no snapshot test on exact prompt string.
- **Scope-creep risk:** File-ops extraction, retry, incremental merge are explicitly out of scope — file as separate work items (already R2/R3/R5) rather than expanding this item.

Logic/retry/file-ops are R2/R3/R5. Source: `docs/session-compaction-pi-comparison.md` §5.1 R1 and work-item Implementation Notes.

## Goal
Add incremental summarization support so proxy compaction merges new information into the previous summary rather than always generating fresh summaries.

## Background
From the compaction comparison (LP-0MTT890RO000AEQM): Pi merges new information into the existing summary using an `UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT` when a previous compaction exists. The proxy always generates a fresh summary from scratch, losing continuity across compaction events.

**Gap score:** MEDIUM severity — if a session compacts multiple times, each new summary starts from scratch rather than building on the previous one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: The proxy detects when a previous compaction summary exists for the session
- [ ] AC2: When a previous summary exists, the summarizer uses an incremental/merge prompt that updates the existing summary
- [ ] AC3: The incremental prompt preserves all sections from the previous summary and updates only changed/new sections
- [ ] AC4: When no previous summary exists, the summarizer uses the standard full summary prompt
- [ ] AC5: The previous summary is stored in session state and passed through the compaction pipeline
- [ ] AC6: All existing compaction tests continue to pass
- [ ] AC7: Unit tests added for both full and incremental summarization paths
- [ ] AC8: Document the summary lifecycle (creation → incremental updates → reset on new session)

## Implementation Notes
- Requires storing the last compaction summary in session state (slot-cache or session metadata)
- Requires an "update" prompt variant similar to Pi's `UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT`
- The prompt should instruct the model to merge new information while preserving existing context
- Expected effort: ~4-8 hours
- This is the largest remaining gap item

# Intake Brief — Provide Pi-aligned system prompt for proxy compaction summarizer (R1 companion)

## Problem Statement
Proxy-side compaction summarization uses a generic system prompt (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — “Summarise the middle portion… Neutral concise style… No preamble”) that predates Pi's proven guard-railed prompt. Pi's `SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (`@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` `dist/core/compaction/utils.js`) is a tight, role-defining system prompt that explicitly prevents the model from continuing the conversation or answering questions and scopes it to “ONLY output the structured summary”. Adopting Pi's system prompt closes the remaining system-role quality gap alongside R1's user-prompt replacement and ensures the structured template (Goal / Constraints / Progress / Decisions / Next Steps / Critical Context) is interpreted as a summarization task, not a conversation turn.

Without this, even after R1's structured user prompt lands, the summarizer’s system role still carries the old generic instruction (“suitable for feeding into a subsequent LLM prompt”) rather than Pi's explicit `Do NOT continue / Do NOT respond / ONLY output` guard rails, risking continuation behavior and format drift — especially on Qwen3 local and the upcoming `compact` (Muse → DeepSeek) remote path.

## Users
- **Proxy operator / local-model user** — gets compacted summaries that reliably follow the requested structured format instead of continuing the chat or adding preamble.
- **Agent-framework consumer whose session was compacted** — downstream LLM receives a clean, parseable summary without invented continuations.
- **Operator customizing compaction** — can override the system prompt locally without forking code (see Mechanism).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 — System prompt matches Pi:** `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (consumed by `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py:build_local_summarizer` as the `system` message) is replaced with Pi's `SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT` verbatim (or semantically identical wording):
  > `You are a context summarization assistant. Your task is to read a conversation between a user and an AI coding assistant, then produce a structured summary following the exact format specified.`
  > `Do NOT continue the conversation. Do NOT respond to any questions in the conversation. ONLY output the structured summary.`
  Source: `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/compaction/utils.js:SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (`@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`, also documented in `docs/compaction.md`) and `dist/core/compaction/compaction.js:generateSummary` wiring via `completeSimple(..., { systemPrompt: SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT })`.
- [ ] **AC2 — Guard rails preserved:** Prompt contains the exact guard rails: `Do NOT continue the conversation. Do NOT respond to any questions` and `ONLY output the structured summary` (case/punctuation may vary only if semantically identical; prefer verbatim Pi string to avoid drift).
- [ ] **AC3 — Mechanism documented / optionally file-backed:** Implementation notes the available custom-system-prompt mechanism and either (a) keeps the constant as single source of truth (simplest, matches R1) with a rationale comment, **or** (b) additionally exposes a file-backed override for operator customization:
  - Option B: add `proxy/prompts/compaction-summarizer.txt` (UTF-8, < 64 KB, repo default) containing Pi's system prompt and wire loading via `proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py` (`resolve_system_prompt` precedence: `.sorraAgents/prompts/<alias>.txt` override → repo default `system_prompt.file`) or a lightweight direct file read in `compaction_summarizer.py`/`provider.py`. If Option B is chosen, `proxy/config.yaml` (and `config-cheap.yaml`/`config-fast.yaml` if applicable) need not gain a `models.compact.system_prompt` entry unless the `compact` remote model (LP-0MTT0O74N009E7N2) is the execution path — document the choice.
  - Either option must handle missing/oversized file fail-open (log warning, fall back to Pi constant) per `prompt_resolver` conventions (`MAX_PROMPT_SIZE=64KB`).
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression in compaction tests:** All existing compaction tests continue to pass (`proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py` — asserts `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is non-empty/string and `compaction_config().summarizer_system_prompt`; `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py` — asserts system message equals the constant; `proxy/tests/test_compaction_dry_run.py` etc.). Tests that assert prompt content are updated to the new Pi string or made agnostic.
- [ ] **AC5 — Rationale comment + docs:** The change is documented with a brief rationale comment above `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `provider.py` referencing Pi's `SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and the gap analysis (parent LP-0MTT890RO000AEQM / R1 LP-0MTTPXHTI0081WIR). Prompt file header (if added) cites the same source. Related docs/code comments affected by the prompt change are updated (e.g., docstring in `compaction_config()`).
- [ ] **AC6 — Full suite / dry-run unaffected:** Full project test suite passes; `compaction_dry_run` and `decide_session_compaction` paths are unchanged (prompt change only, summarizer remains fail-open, timeout/max_tokens unchanged).

## Constraints
- Prompt-engineering change only — no summarizer retry, file-ops extraction, or incremental-merge logic (R2 LP-0MTTPXI1Y003YFOU, R3 LP-0MTTPXIAB0031AC4, R5 LP-0MTTPXIIX005Y0Z9 are separate).
- Must remain fail-open: HTTP/timeout/parse behavior in `compaction_summarizer.py:build_local_summarizer` unchanged (returns `""` on error).
- Keep `max_tokens` / `summarizer_ctx_size` as-is (512 / 8192 via `compaction_config`); verbosity controlled by system+user prompts, not budget changes here.
- If file-backed, reuse existing `prompt_resolver` infra (no new deps); local override dir is `.sorraAgents/prompts/` (git-ignored, project-local).

## Existing State
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:674-681` defines `_SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` as:
  ```
  "Summarise the middle portion of this conversation for context retention. "
  "Preserve essential instructions, decisions, and key facts. "
  "Omit routine back-and-forth, acknowledgments, and redundant context. "
  "Write in a neutral, concise style suitable for feeding into a subsequent "
  "LLM prompt. Do NOT include any preamble or closing remarks."
  ```
  and `compaction_config()` returns it as `summarizer_system_prompt`.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py:79` imports it as `from proxy.provider import _SUMMARIZER_SYSTEM_PROMPT as _prompt` and sends it as the `system` message with the transcript (`_transcript_for_summarizer`) as `user`. No `<conversation>` wrapping, no `previousSummary`, no template in user role (R1 addresses the user template; this item addresses the system role).
- Pi (`@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`):
  - `dist/core/compaction/utils.js:150` — `export const SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT = "You are a context summarization assistant… Do NOT continue… ONLY output…"`
  - `dist/core/compaction/compaction.js:435-459` — `generateSummary` builds user content as `<conversation>...</conversation>` + optional `<previous-summary>...</previous-summary>` + `SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT`/`UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT`, and calls `completeSimple(model, { systemPrompt: SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT, messages: summarizationMessages })`. Guard rails live in the system prompt; the structured sections live in the user prompt.
  - `docs/compaction.md` documents the same split.
- Custom-system-prompt mechanism available in proxy:
  - `proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py` — `resolve_system_prompt(alias, model_cfg)` / `validate_prompt_config` / `compose_messages` / `MAX_PROMPT_SIZE=64KB` / `OVERRIDE_DIR=.sorraAgents/prompts` + `REPO_ROOT/proxy/prompts/*.txt` (e.g., `assistant.txt`, `author.txt`). # Intake Brief — Unknown errors from Muse (LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS)

**Work Item:** LP-0MTV77DAT0018ZUS
**Type:** bug
**Priority:** critical

**Headline:** Muse (opencode.ai/zen/go) upstream frequently stalls mid-stream (240s idle), emitting `stall_after_content` / `stall_exhausted` errors that neither Pi nor the proxy recovers automatically — operator must type `continue` to retry, after which the same stall often recurs.

## Problem Statement

Sessions routed to `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` via `opencode-go` (endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go`, Responses API translation) experience frequent upstream stalls. The proxy retries pre-content stalls up to 3× with backoff (2/4/8s), but **after any content has been delivered** (`stall_after_content`, 240s idle) it terminates the stream with a synthetic error chunk (`error_type: stall_after_content`, `suggested_action: "Retry the request with full context, or route to a healthier provider"`) and does **not** automatically re-dispatch to a sibling/DeepSeek provider. The client (Pi / herdr) surfaces this as a hard error requiring manual `continue`. Example session `herdr-1788968078-174711-604` (and others today: `herdr-1789022401-3563001-26239`, `herdr-1789023032-3566868-12685`) show dozens of `Upstream ReadTimeout` → retry cycles, periodic `max retries exhausted` and `stall_after_content` terminal errors. Other error classes observed the same window include `stall_exhausted` and `stream_exception` (local Qwen3 `RemoteProtocolError`). `continue` works transiently because it re-issues the request with a fresh retry budget (often landing on another `opencode-go` entry or after cooldown expiry).

## Users

- **Agent operator (you)** — running long Pi `plan` sessions (60–125k estimated tokens); needs the proxy/Pi to self-heal stalls without manual `continue` interruptions.
- **Pi/herdr agent user** — expects tool-calling `plan` sessions to progress unattended; stalls block task progress and waste wall-clock time (each stall costs 240s idle + retry backoffs).
- **Proxy operator** — needs clear error taxonomy and actionable handling (auto-fallback, circuit-breaker, compaction) instead of repeated identical upstream retries.

### User Stories

- As an operator, when Muse stalls mid-stream I want the proxy (or Pi) to automatically retry/route to a healthy sibling provider with full context so I don't have to type `continue` manually.
- As an operator, I want RCA + a fix proposal that classifies all error kinds from `herdr-1788968078-174711-604` (and any other kinds found) and maps each to an owner/handler (Pi vs proxy vs upstream).
- As a reviewer, I want acceptance criteria that prove the dominant stall is eliminated or auto-recovered and that context growth stops exacerbating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Error taxonomy & evidence:** The work item (or linked doc/comment) lists every distinct error class observed for `herdr-1788968078-174711-604` and across the 2026-09-10 window (at minimum: `Upstream ReadTimeout` pre-content retry, `stall_after_content` 240s after-content, `stall_exhausted` / `max retries exhausted`, `stream_exception` local `RemoteProtocolError`, and `context_pressure` / `context_too_large` routing signals), each with a short log exemplar and approximate count for the reference session, plus any additional class discovered in the broader scan.
2. **AC2 — RCA for "requires manual continue":** Documents why the proxy does not auto-recover `stall_after_content` (post-content retry is deliberately disabled at `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py:_handle_remote_streaming` → yields terminal error chunk instead of re-dispatch), why no healthy fallback is available in many of these stalls (all three `opencode-go` entries share one failure domain `https://opencode.ai/zen/go` and are skipped together; DeepSeek `api.deepseek.com` is gated by `available_times: ["00:00-01:00","04:00-06:00","10:00-00:00"]` and unavailable off-window, leaving the chain effectively exhausted), and why context magnifies the failure (compaction is `dry_run: true`, so the session grows 62k→125k unchecked; large prompts already bypass local `cold_threshold 38000` / `warm_threshold 83285` → every request is forced to Muse with no local fallback).
3. **AC3 — Fix proposal (actionable, not speculative):** Proposes at least two concrete changes with trade-offs and owner (proxy vs Pi): (a) **Auto-recovery for post-content stalls** — either proxy-side transparent re-dispatch of `stall_after_content` to the next healthy provider in the chain (using buffered-prefix / full-context replay) or Pi-side auto-`continue` on `error_type: stall_after_content`/`stall_exhausted` without user input; must not require manual `continue`. (b) **Context mitigation** — e.g., enabling live compaction (flip `compaction_dry_run: false`) or imposing a context cap / compaction enforcement so sessions don't grow past the per-slot budget and keep hitting the stall-prone large-prompt path. Includes config/code touch points and rollout risk notes.
4. **AC4 — Verification plan:** Describes how to confirm the fix without manual `continue`: replay or shadow the reference session log, or induce a synthetic stall; demonstrates that the same prompt history now completes (or automatically re-tries to DeepSeek/local) and that the proxy no longer emits a terminal `stall_after_content` requiring operator action.
5. **AC5 — Documentation updated:** Work-item findings and the chosen fix path recorded (description or linked doc/comment); no silent retry that hides billing/upstream health — any auto-recovery must still log `suggested_action` and increment stall metrics for observability.

**Constraints**

- Must use evidence from the live deployment (proxy.log, `proxy/config.yaml` provider chain, `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` stall paths) — no invented upstream behavior.
- Respect `available_times` economics for DeepSeek; any proposal must account for off-window unavailability.
- Keep the proxy's `upstream_idle_timeout_seconds: 240` and `upstream_retry_max_attempts: 3` as baseline; tuning them is allowed only with rationale.
- No speculative "upstream is down" claims without log entry (available_times, Muse 429s, etc.).

**Existing State**

- Provider chain for `models.plan` (and `author`/`code`): `local-qwen3 (Qwen3) → opencode-go-3/2/1 (muse-spark-1.2-contributor @ https://opencode.ai/zen/go, api: openai-responses) → deepseek-v4-flash @ https://api.deepseek.com` (timed). Responses-API translation via `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` + `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- Retry layers: Tier-1 per-stream pre-content retry (`upstream_retry_max_attempts: 3`, base 2s), Tier-2 60s `provider_cooldown`, Tier-3 stall circuit breaker (`window 300s, threshold 3, cooldown 180s`), failure-domain grouping (`LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F` — same endpoint skips all siblings), plus sibling-fallback and `chain_hold` (300s, 3 cycles).
- Stall handling: `proxy_remote.py:_handle_remote_streaming` ~line 1880 emits `stall_after_content` without retry once any content streamed; `stall_exhausted` after 3 idle retries. Daily log shows ~132 `Upstream ReadTimeout` and ~12–15 `stall_after_content`/`stall_exhausted` terminals across several sessions including the flagged `herdr-1788968078-174711-604`; `context_pressure` warnings appear once `estimated_tokens > 0.80 × per_slot_ctx` (e.g., 109k > 83285).
- Compaction: `server.compaction_dry_run: true`, `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0.70`, physical per-slot cap `83285` (fast) / `100000` (cheap) → flagged session never compacts, grows unchecked.

**Desired Change**

- Deliver RCA + fix proposal meeting AC1–AC3, file the chosen fix as follow-up work item(s) with clear owner (proxy vs Pi) and acceptance criteria per AC4–AC5. No implementation is required in this intake; `pending` → `verified` moves to the follow-up item(s).

**Key Files (predicted)**

- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` — `_handle_remote_streaming`, idle/stall retry paths, `stall_after_content` terminal branch, `_check_stall_circuit_breaker`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — stall circuit breaker, failure-domain grouping, cooldowns.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `models.plan` provider chain, `available_times` for DeepSeek, `upstream_idle_timeout_seconds: 240`, `compaction_dry_run: true`.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` — evidence source (session `herdr-1788968078-174711-604` and broader 2026-09-10 taxonomy).
- Optional companion: Pi-side stream error handling (herdr/Pi agent retry on `error_type: stall_after_content`).

**Related Work**

- LP-0MSF1PUM90099ZSW — Proactively fall back on mid-stream stalls (completed) — context for "tell client to retry vs proactive fallback".
- LP-0MSDRRDWK009QT4E — Recovery-first silent continue for pre-content failures (completed).
- LP-0MTPMF03P0046MFG — Switch to sibling provider after repeated upstream failures (completed).
- LP-0MTGB... / compaction items — dry_run advisory logging, live compaction wiring; directly related to context mitigation prong.
- LP-0MTV5GFL8007WSK2 — Fix compaction dry-run logging (open, critical) — shares the same `compaction_dry_run` root cause.

**Risks & Assumptions**

- **Assumption: Off-window DeepSeek unavailable** → at many stall timestamps DeepSeek `available_times` window is closed, leaving no healthy remote fallback — verified from config; if operator widens the window the fallback picture changes.
- **Risk: Post-content auto-retry complexity** — re-dispatching after partial content risks duplicate tool calls / billing; proposal must define idempotency guard (replay full context, discard partial prefix, or buffer before yield).
- **Risk: Raising idle timeout vs false stalls** — DeepSeek reasoning pauses already forced 240s (LP-0MSF5I7XN009ENWQ); raising further slows true failure detection.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Do not expand to unrelated inference tuning; file separate items for upstream health monitoring vs per-model routing.
- **Assumption: User's "continue works, then fails again"** equals proxy's 240s stall → terminal error → manual continue issues new request with fresh retry budget, which succeeds until next large-prompt stall.

**Related Work (automated report)**

- See "Related Work" above; taxonomy search seeded from `Muse opencode stall` matched LP-0MTPMF03P0046MFG / LP-0MSF1PUM90099ZSW / LP-0MSDRRDWK009QT4E.

Source: this session reply.

- Q: none — Answer: n/a. Additional research (proxy.log 2026-09-10, `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` stall paths) was sufficient to draft RCA without further interview; re-asking about Muses's health would duplicate log evidence.

## Goal / user story

As a proxy operator, I want failure-domain exclusion to distinguish gateway-wide outages from model-specific failures, so unreachable gateways are skipped efficiently while independently healthy models behind a reachable router are still tried.

## Context

This is the follow-up refinement to the simple per-model failure-domain fix. Always scoping by model can waste time when the gateway itself is unreachable: every model entry may be tried with retries/backoff against a dead endpoint before moving to another gateway.

## Scope: hierarchical solution

Refine failure exclusion by error class:

- Connection-level failures indicating the gateway itself is unreachable (`ConnectError`, `ConnectTimeout`, DNS failures, refused/unreachable gateway): exclude the whole endpoint failure domain.
- Request-level failures after reaching the gateway (`ReadTimeout` after connection established, HTTP 5xx, `finish_reason:error`, empty/zero-content responses, and similar model/route-level failures): exclude only the endpoint-plus-model scope.
- Keep usage-limit quarantine per API-key account, unchanged.
- Make the sibling-fallback circuit breaker and brand/entry cooldown checks consistent with the hierarchical scope.

Likely touch points in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:

- `_failure_domain_key()` model scoping from the predecessor item
- failure classification for connection-level versus request-level errors
- `attempted_domains` call sites in fallback cycles
- `_record_sibling_failure()` / `_entry_cooldown_key()`
- tests in `tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` plus new hierarchical error-class cases.

## Goal / user story

As a proxy operator, I want a single empty-response to not poison the whole failure domain, so that sibling API keys on the same endpoint (which have independent usage limits) are still tried before falling through to another gateway.

## Context / evidence

- Currently a single `empty_response` adds the endpoint to `attempted_domains` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4545`), skipping all same-endpoint siblings per-request — e.g. one empty response on `opencode-go-2` blocked `opencode-go` and `opencode-go-3` on 2026-09-10.
- Sibling keys have independent usage-limit accounts, so retrying them is not always futile; only the endpoint itself is suspect.
- Related: `_record_sibling_failure()` already uses a streak threshold (default 2) before extended cooldown — domain poisoning should be consistent with that.

## Scope

Likely touch points in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:

- Empty-response handling in `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` / `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (around lines 4545, 5518-5556).
- Only add to `attempted_domains` on the 2nd consecutive `empty_response` for that endpoint+model within the request (or when the sibling-failure streak threshold is reached).
- Keep `ReadTimeout`/`stream_error`/`HTTP 5xx` domain poisoning on first failure (unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

1. A single `empty_response` on one entry does NOT skip same-endpoint siblings in the same request; the next sibling is tried.
2. Two consecutive `empty_response` failures on the same endpoint+model DO poison the domain (siblings skipped, matching current behavior for confirmed-bad gateways).
3. `ReadTimeout`/`stream_error`/`HTTP 5xx` still poison the domain on first failure.
4. New/updated tests cover first-empty-tries-sibling and second-empty-poisons-domain; relevant proxy test suites pass.

# Surface proxy-side compaction metadata in responses (Pi client bridge)

Enable the Pi coding-agent client to keep its dispatched view consistent
with the proxy's compacted session history, without client modifications.
Today the proxy compacts server-side (parent LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD machinery)
but the compaction decision and the injected summary marker are invisible
to the client: Pi keeps sending its full un-compacted history, which
forces history_mismatch fallbacks and CREATION re-summarization on every
turn (churn). This item adds the wire signal; the client-side consumer
lives in the SorraAgents project (Pi extension work item, cross-
referenced in Notes).

## User Story

As a Pi client user, I want the proxy to tell me when it compacted my
session and what the compacted view looks like, so my client can dispatch
the same compacted history and the proxy can resume incremental
(summarize-first) compaction instead of re-summarizing from scratch.

## Design

Flow:

    Turn N:  proxy compacts session history to
               [system, first_user, summary_marker, recent...]
             sets response headers:
               X-Compaction-Occurred: true
               X-Compaction-Marker: <base64 of exact marker content>
               X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized: <n>
               X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept: <n>
    Client extension (SorraAgents) reads headers, mirrors the view in
    its dispatch layer on the next turn (JSONL storage untouched).

Changes:

1. `proxy/router_helpers.py` `_handle_session`: when compaction is applied
   (`result["compaction_applied"] = True`), additionally surface
   `compaction_summary_text`, `compaction_turns_summarized`,
   `compaction_recent_turns_kept` on the session result, taken from the
   `decide_session_compaction` plan dict (`_compaction`).
2. `proxy/router.py`: after `outgoing_headers` is assembled (near the
   `X-Resolved-Model` header), when compaction was applied, add the four
   headers. The marker is built from the proxy's exact
   `_SUMMARY_MARKER` / `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END` delimiters
   (`compaction.py`) so the client never has to replicate the marker
   format (no drift).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When live compaction is applied for a request, the response
  includes `X-Compaction-Occurred: true` plus `X-Compaction-Marker`,
  `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`, `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept`.
- AC2: The marker header content decodes to the exact message content
  the proxy injected into the compacted history (verbatim, including
  delimiters).
- AC3: Non-compaction responses (noop / below-trigger / dry-run /
  remote_with_guidance) set none of these headers.
- AC4: Header emission is fail-safe: any error surfaces no compaction
  headers and never changes dispatch behaviour — the header block is
  additive only, after compaction has already been applied.
- AC5: Headers survive streaming responses (SSE) — set on the outgoing
  `StreamingResponse`, not inside the streamed body.
- AC6: Unit tests cover the header contract: applied-compaction,
  dry-run, noop, remote_with_guidance, and marker round-trip
  (encode → decode → equals injected message content).

## Notes / related

- Companion work item (client extension): SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 in the
  SorraAgents project.
- Reuses the existing compaction plan fields (`summary_text`,
  `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`) already returned by
  `plan_session_compaction` — no changes to compaction logic itself.
- Delivers the dispatch-base contract required by the durability item
  LP-0MTXGU9N1009QNSB (server-side compaction not durable across turns);
  that item now depends on this one.
- End-to-end prerequisite: LP-0MTXEBQ4E001BMI2 (local HTTP 400 on
  compacted history). The bridge itself is not gated on it, but the
  durability outcome is.
- Superseded items retired 2026-09-12: LP-0MTXGUAPN003WI0W (Pi client
  compaction never fires) and LP-0MTXGUBG9005V7IW (instrument frozen
  pre_tokens anomaly).
- Header size caveat: summaries are base64'd into one header; if real
  summaries exceed a few KB, revisit with a sidecar endpoint
  (`GET /sessions/<id>/compaction`).
data.title: Surface proxy-side compaction metadata in responses (Pi client bridge)

## Problem
Deleting a test file during implementation makes the changed-scope test selection fail with pytest exit code 4 ('file or directory not found'), which aborts 'implement.py finish' at its changed-scope gate.

Repro: work item LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V removed proxy/tests/test_slot_scheduler.py. The changed-scope command built by the test skill became:

  pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings <...modified test files...> proxy/tests/test_slot_scheduler.py

(test_slot_scheduler.py no longer exists) -> pytest exits 4 with no test failures collected, so implement.py finish reports 'Test run failed' and enters the interactive test-fix prompt.

## Root cause
.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py: map_changed_to_tests() enumerates changed files from git and, for any changed file matching test-file naming (_is_test_file), adds it to the selection WITHOUT verifying it still exists:
    if _is_test_file(rel):
        selected.add(changed_file)
        continue
Deleted test files are therefore always selected.

## Expected
Deleted test files must be excluded from the changed-scope selection (skip when not (project_root / changed_file).exists()). The selection should also guard against other non-existent paths.

## Impact
Any implementation that removes/renames a test file cannot pass the implement.py changed-scope gate without an IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND override that forces full scope.

## Files
- .pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py (map_changed_to_tests)
- .pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py (_run_changed_scope_pytest)

## Problem
Auditing an already-committed + already-merged work item runs the code-quality (ruff) scan over the ENTIRE repo instead of the item's changed files. Any pre-existing critical/high ruff finding then blocks the audit with "Ready to close: No", even though the audited change did not introduce it.

Observed on LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V (slot-config simplification, commit d3e08692, already on origin/dev): the audit flagged 8 pre-existing ruff findings in files untouched by the item (proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py I001, proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py F841, proxy/tests/test_empty_response_body_snippet.py I001 + 4x F841, proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py F841) and demoted all ACs to partial, skipping Phase 2.

## Root cause
audit_runner.py computes the cq scope via _git_changed_files(), which reads  + . After implement.py finish commits and pushes (the normal flow), the main checkout is clean and HEAD == the delivered commit, so the changed list is EMPTY. run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None) then treats None as 'scan everything' and lints the whole repo.

## Expected
When the working tree is clean and the item's work is already merged, the cq scan should scope to the item's delivered files (e.g. from the merge-gate verified commits: ), not fall back to the whole repo. At minimum, an empty changed-file list should not silently widen to a full-repo scan for an already-merged item.

## Impact
Every audit of an already-merged item inherits repo-wide pre-existing lint debt and can be blocked by unrelated findings; this also makes the false-positive screen / remediation loop operate on files outside the item scope.

## Files
- .pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py (_git_changed_files, code-quality scan call sites ~8083-8096)

## Summary
The local dispatch gate admits more concurrent generating sessions than `session_slot_pool_size`. Observed live on 2026-09-13 ~21:15-21:16 IST (fast mode, `session_slot_pool_size: 1`): two agent sessions (`01a09c62-4057-77eb-98a9-9bcca77cd660`, plan model; `herdr-1789330141-3165053-7515`) were both generating on local Qwen3 at once, and the proxy logged `local_dispatch_denied ... owner=01a09c62-4057-77eb-98a9-9bcca77cd660 active=2` (`/tmp/proxy-startup2.log`). Backend llama-server (PID 975372, port 45201) is `--parallel 1`, so the two admitted streams are serialized/interleaved, inflating TTFT to ~11-14 s (vs 0.6-3 s uncontended at 21:08).

## Evidence
- `local_dispatch_denied session=herdr-1789326164-3152185-18806 owner=01a09c62-4057-77eb-98a9-9bcca77cd660 active=2` (21:15:45, 21:16:46, 21:16:52, 21:16:54).
- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` 11-14 s while both sessions cycle request->tool_call->request; 654-3000 ms when only one session active.
- `active=` is the 3rd return of `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, which in the generating-state branch is `_generating_count` (`proxy/router_helpers.py` ~L1386-1400).

## Likely mechanism (generating-only pool over-subscription)
1. Occupancy is generating-only (`local_generating_queries`, LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N): a session counts only from first token to stream end; prefill and post-stream cooldown do not count (`proxy/server.py` L105-120; `proxy/provider.py` L2692-2771).
2. The prefill-aware guard (LP-0MTJET4I5009EHNX) caps concurrent prefills at `max_local`, BUT the whole cap check is skipped when the session already holds a lease: `if not own_has_lease:` (`proxy/router_helpers.py` ~L1386). Same-session re-acquisition is always permitted (no-preemption), and a 30 s inactive cooldown lease still satisfies `own_has_lease`.
3. Once two sessions each hold a lease, neither the generating cap nor the prefill cap is re-checked for them; the generating counter (incremented at first byte) is the only brake, so both can be generating at once -> `active=2 > max_local=1`.
4. Inactive leases are deliberately ignored by the generating-only pool (so `occupied_by_others` is unused in that branch), letting a second session slip in during the first's inter-request gap.

## Impact
Cost/latency regression: users see 11-14 s TTFT on a backend that should serve one stream at a time; contradicts the documented `session_slot_pool_size` semantics and the prior session that asked 'Why are there three active slots right now?'.

## Acceptance criteria
- With `session_slot_pool_size: N`, the proxy never reports `active=2` (or >N) generating sessions, including when sessions already hold inactive leases.
- Re-acquisition by a lease-holding session still respects the generating/prefill cap (or is documented as intentional with the effect on TTFT quantified).
- Regression test reproduces two leased sessions cycling requests and asserts the generating count never exceeds `max_local`.
- No regression in false-full `local_concurrency_limit` fallback rate (LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N baseline).

## References
- LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N (generating-only pool), LP-0MTJET4I5009EHNX (prefill-aware guard)
- `proxy/router_helpers.py` `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, `proxy/server.py` counters, `proxy/config-fast.yaml` (1 slot, queue depth 3/45 s)
- Prior session: 01a09a45-ab19-73d6-9e47-8ea37b5d4f5f
data.title: Bug: generating-only slot pool over-subscribes local Qwen (active=2 with session_slot_pool_size=1)

## Goal
Decide and implement the correct local routing threshold now that the local profile runs one slot with 262144 ctx.

## Findings
- local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold is 100000 (proxy/config.yaml).
- The runtime clamp is effective_warm_clamp = min(warm_config, effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx_size, slots)) and effective_per_slot_threshold = ctx_size // slots - 4096 (proxy/proxy/provider.py). With ctx_size 262144 and slots 1 that is 258048, so the clamp yields min(100000, 258048) = 100000.
- The clamp is a cap, not an expansion: more context per slot does NOT raise the threshold. The configured 100000 is the binding value.
- Consequence: 1982 routing_skip_local reason=context_too_large events on 2026-09-14, pushing large sessions onto the remote tier.
- The compaction trigger is 0.70 x 100000 = 70000, i.e. below the local routing threshold, so sessions above the trigger are meant to be compacted rather than routed remote - but compaction is currently failing (separate item).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded for the intended local warm threshold at 1 slot x 262144 ctx (keep 100000 vs raise toward the physical cap), including prefill cost, KV read cost and slot-occupancy trade-offs.
- [ ] If changed, the value and the compaction trigger are set so the trigger sits below the routing threshold.
- [ ] The effective threshold is logged at startup so operators can confirm the runtime value.
- [ ] Tests assert the clamp semantics (min only, never expansion).
- [ ] Full test suite green.
data.title: Local large-context routing threshold does not scale with per-slot capacity (100K vs 258K at 1 slot)
